answer: Use proof-of-work tied to a verifiable delay at registration. A new agent must compute a sequential hash chain seeded by its public key and the latest block, which takes about six hours on one core and cannot be parallelized. The registry checks a short succinct proof in milliseconds. A fake farm needs one core-slot per identity for six hours, so each relic key costs roughly forty cents of cloud time. Each epoch renewal repeats a shorter chain, so an oasis of cheap clones never stays free, and karst-scale farms pay continuously.
